subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint — POC milestone owners, acceptance criteria, blockers
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@acmeanalytics.com>; Acme Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint — POC milestone owners, acceptance criteria, blockers

Hi Elena / procurement team —

Quick MAP checkpoint for this week as we push toward the POC close. Highlights below (short & action-oriented). I copied the internal owners so they're looped for commitments.

1) Acceptance criteria (final draft attached: MAP_v2.xlsx)
   - Latency: 95th percentile inference < 250ms for 512-token prompts
   - Throughput: sustain 10 concurrent sessions at 1000 tokens/min per session
   - Quality: pass our eval suite with >= 92% intent-match on the 150-case test set
   - Security: SOC-equivalent audit evidence for data handling in place

2) Current blockers
   - Security questionnaire: procurement requested clarifications on retention settings (see note below) — procurement
   - Eval variance: a handful of edge cases failing on short-context prompts — Marissa to investigate
   - Model mismatch: quantized 8-bit variant shows minor hallucination patterns on numeric tables — Karthik / Priyom investigating

3) Near-term asks (this week)
   - Elena: confirm target date for procurement sign-off by 2027-07-27
   - Marissa: deliver updated eval log (eval-testcases.csv) by 2027-07-16
   - Karthik: share a mitigation plan for quantization drift by 2027-07-19

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (mutual action plan), eval-testcases.csv (current failing cases).

Proposed next sync: Wed 2027-07-21 10:00 PT — 30 minutes to go over acceptance checklist and any redlines. If procurement needs separate time, let me know.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: eval-testcases.csv (csv)]

Sean — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick notes from procurement / security side: 

- Procurement wants the retention window spelled out in the MAP (how long logs and prompts are kept). Can you add the default and the customer-configurable options?
- On SOC evidence: we need the signed questionnaire back by 2027-07-22 to hit our internal review cycle. Can your security team confirm?
- For the acceptance criteria: the throughput target looks good but we need clarification on how burst capacity will be handled (will there be throttling or queued requests?).

I'll plan for the Wed 07/21 sync but would like a 10-minute pre-brief with Sean and Marissa to align on the security/retention language.

Best,
Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Morris <elena@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP checkpoint — POC milestone owners, acceptance criteria, blockers

Elena / team — quick technical update on the quantization drift blocker. Summary: the 8-bit quantized variant exhibits higher token-level entropy on numeric table paraphrasing; it's causing the minor hallucinations Marissa observed. Root cause looks like an attention scaling mismatch in the current quant path when sequence length < 64.

Mitigation plan (short):
- Short term (this week): deploy a model wrapper that forces FP16 kernel for short-context requests (adds ~15ms, keeps latency within SLA for targeted flows).
- Medium term: we have a patch to the kernel selection logic to skip the problematic optimized kernel for these sequences; target code drop on 2027-07-26.

Owner commitments:
- Karthik: implement and validate the FP16 wrapper by 2027-07-19 (done)
- Priyom: confirm autoscaler policy to absorb the small CPU/GPU overhead by 2027-07-18 (in progress)

I validated the wrapper on the eval set and the intent-match score recovered from 89% -> 93% on the failing subset. Will share perf numbers in the Wed sync.

— Karthik

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@acmeanalytics.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP checkpoint — POC milestone owners, acceptance criteria, blockers

Elena — thanks for the quick responses and procurement heads-up. Quick decisions / confirmations before the Wed sync: 

- Security retention language: confirmed — default 30/90; customer can request 0 days (Marissa to attach the signed policy first thing Monday).
- Quantization mitigation: Karthik's FP16 wrapper validated; Marissa's re-eval shows pass rate improvement. We'll keep the wrapper active for short-context flows until the kernel fix is in.
- Autoscaling / burst behavior: Priyom confirms autoscaler will queue bursts beyond sustained throughput with an optional burst window; we'll document throttling behavior in the MAP appendix.

Next steps: 07/21 sync remains. I'll prepare a one-page acceptance checklist for quick sign-off during the call and route the formal MAP + signed security packet to procurement afterwards.

If procurement can sign off on the proposed retention and the one-page checklist in the call, we should be on track to close the POC and move to pilot by the end of July.

Thanks all —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
